examples.solution_text:
Factorise the common factor $x$.
$\begin{align*}x(a+b)&=8\\x&=\frac{8}{a+b}\end{align*}$
This requires $a+b\ne0$. If $a+b=0$, the original equation has no solution.

Keep the subtraction when factorising.
$\begin{align*}t(p-q)&=9\\t&=\frac{9}{p-q}\end{align*}$
This requires $p\ne q$. If $p=q$, the original equation has no solution.

The term $2a$ contributes $2$ inside the bracket.
$\begin{align*}a(b+2)&=c\\a&=\frac{c}{b+2}\end{align*}$
This requires $b\ne-2$. If $b=-2$, there is no solution when $c\ne0$, and every $a$ is allowed when $c=0$.

Collect the $x$ terms, then factorise.
$\begin{align*}ax-mx+3y&=8y\\ax-mx&=5y\\x(a-m)&=5y\\x&=\frac{5y}{a-m}\end{align*}$
This requires $a\ne m$. If $a=m$, there is no solution when $y\ne0$, and every $x$ is allowed when $y=0$.

Expand both brackets before collecting the $x$ terms.
$\begin{align*}bx+4b&=ax+3a\\bx-ax&=3a-4b\\x(b-a)&=3a-4b\\x&=\frac{3a-4b}{b-a}\end{align*}$
This requires $b\ne a$. If $b=a\ne0$, there is no solution. If $a=b=0$, every $x$ is allowed.

Multiply every term by $a$, then collect and factorise.
$\begin{align*}4+ab&=ac\\4&=ac-ab\\4&=a(c-b)\\a&=\frac{4}{c-b}\end{align*}$
This requires $c\ne b$, and the result is nonzero. If $c=b$, the original equation has no solution.

Clear the denominator, expand, then collect and factorise.
$\begin{align*}y(x-2)&=3x+4\\xy-2y&=3x+4\\xy-3x&=4+2y\\x(y-3)&=4+2y\\x&=\frac{4+2y}{y-3}\end{align*}$
This requires $y\ne3$. The result cannot equal $2$, so the original denominator restriction is satisfied. If $y=3$, there is no solution.

examples.question_text: Make $a$ the subject of $\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}=\frac{1}{2c}$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are nonzero.
examples.solution_text:
Multiply every term by $2abc$, then collect and factorise.
$\begin{align*}2bc+2ac&=ab\\2bc&=ab-2ac\\2bc&=a(b-2c)\\a&=\frac{2bc}{b-2c}\end{align*}$
This requires $b\ne2c$. Since $b$ and $c$ are nonzero, the result is nonzero. If $b=2c$, there is no solution.

examples.derivation: ax+bx=x(a+b)=8, giving x=8/(a+b). When a+b=0, the equation becomes 0=8 and has no solution.
pt-qt=t(p-q)=9, giving t=9/(p-q). When p=q, the equation becomes 0=9 and has no solution.
ab+2a=a(b+2)=c, giving a=c/(b+2). For b=-2, the equation is 0=c: no solution if c is nonzero; every a if c=0.
Subtracting mx and 3y gives ax-mx=5y, hence x(a-m)=5y and x=5y/(a-m). For a=m, 0=5y permits every x exactly when y=0.
Expansion gives bx+4b=ax+3a, so x(b-a)=3a-4b and x=(3a-4b)/(b-a). For a=b, the remaining equation requires a=0; otherwise there is no solution.
Multiplication by nonzero a gives 4+ab=ac, hence 4=a(c-b) and a=4/(c-b). This is nonzero when c differs from b; c=b gives the contradiction 4=0.
Multiplication by x-2 gives xy-2y=3x+4, hence x(y-3)=4+2y and x=(4+2y)/(y-3). Equality to 2 would require 4=-6, so the original restriction holds. For y=3, the equation gives -6=4.
Multiplication by nonzero 2abc gives 2bc+2ac=ab, hence a(b-2c)=2bc and a=2bc/(b-2c). The numerator is nonzero. For b=2c, the equation requires 2bc=0, contradicting the stated restrictions.
